Identity · proposal

Finger Frame

A bracket pair holding a band. Two hands, one on each edge; between them, the slice of the world the app repaints.

Where the shape comes from

The spec describes a rectangle framed by two hands. The capture shows something more specific, and more ownable: a wide, slightly sheared band across the eyes — photographic above and below, illustrated inside. The hands do not surround it. One makes the left edge, one makes the right.

That reading is why the mark is a bracket pair rather than the four corner brackets the current site uses. Corner brackets say crop tool — a shape a hundred apps already own. [ ] says held between two hands, and it happens to be the shape of the app's own initials in the way developers write them.

Durability

Colour is the first thing a brand loses — to a print run, an embroidery machine, a partner's monochrome footer, a system that tints everything one colour. A logo that only works in two colours is a picture, not a mark.

__DURABILITY__
__DURABILITY_SMALL__

The gap between grip and band exists for the one-colour case. Flush, they fuse into a single slab and the mark disappears; with 11 units of ground between them the structure survives every reduction above.

The band is a container

This is what keeps the identity alive without redrawing it. The grip is constant. What sits between the brackets can be flat colour, or a real frame of restyled video — every style the app ships is a new poster without touching the logo.

Lockups

The wordmark

The name is set in the system face — SF Pro on Apple platforms, the page's own stack on the web — semibold, tracked slightly tight, mixed case. It is type, not artwork: nothing is shipped as outlines, and the app, the site and the exported video each set it in whatever the platform provides.

Two custom faces were built for it and neither was better than this. They are kept in tools/ (wordmark_stroked.py, wordmark_typeset.py, wordmark_drawn.py) so the work is recoverable, but nothing imports them.

The mark carries the identity. A neutral, well-hinted face beside it is a legitimate answer, and it is the one in use: it costs nothing to license, renders correctly at every size on every device, and never falls back to something unintended.

The loader

The mark opening, shutting, and turning a quarter — the splash's own moves, on a loop. One cycle: hold shut, the grips part and the band is revealed, hold open, the grips snap shut, then the shut pair swings 90°. Four cycles is a full turn, so the loop is 4 × 1.75s even though the eye reads it at 1.75s.

__LOADER_BIG__
__LOADER_SIZES__

Turning form. Square, because it has to hold the open mark in either orientation.

__LOADER_STRIP__

Full screen to 5×5

It has to work at both ends, and that is not a scaling problem. At 5px the grip stroke is 0.35px and the slot of ground between grip and band is 0.13px: both vanish, and what renders is a grey smudge. The binding feature is the ground, not the stroke — it is the thinnest thing in the mark and the one doing the most work, because with it closed the grips fuse to the band and it stops being a bracket pair at all.

So the geometry is redrawn per size band, the way a type family cuts optical sizes: as the box shrinks, the stroke and the ground get fatter relative to it and the band gives up the room. The cut is chosen by point size, not device pixels — a 10pt mark on a 3× screen has plenty of pixels and is still tiny to the eye.

__LOADER_CUTS__
cut from stroke / ground what changes

Rendered at true pixel size, then blown up — the only honest way to look at this:

__LOADER_TRUEPX__
  • Nothing here is a new shape. It is SplashFrame — the mark at a band width, every other quantity following from it — moving between the same two states the splash's beats 1 and 2 use. Only the band width changes, so the grips keep their exact geometry and merely translate.
  • It turns only while shut. Which is what sizes the box: it needs the open mark at rest, not the circle the open mark's corner would sweep. Below 44pt the turning form falls back to compact rather than turning illegibly.
  • Below 9pt the mark stands down. Three pixels cannot hold five features, and every faithful rendering is a smudge. What still reads is the duo-tone and the fact it is moving, so the square crossfades between the two hues — not a sweeping split, which at 5px is two pixels of travel and reads as nothing.
  • The split holds as a fraction of the band — 39.4% and 54.6% — so the slant does not shear flatter as it opens. SplashView does the same.
  • Two implementations, one animation. BrandLoader.swift and tools/loader.py are checked against each other numerically — 90 values across all three cuts — so they cannot drift into two things that merely look alike.
  • Reduce Motion holds it open and pulses the opacity instead.

Construction

__CONSTRUCTION__
  • Band 372 × 138 in a 512 box — near the 3:1 the real gesture makes.
  • Grip 30 thick, 86 return. At 50 the returns stopped overhanging and it read as two clamps.
  • 11 of ground between grip and band, in every version.
  • Split leans 44 off vertical at 47% — off-centre, so the mark is never quite symmetrical. Neither is the gesture.
  • Whole mark rotated −4°. Level, it goes inert.
  • Clear space on all sides: the grip's return, 86.
